text: A pumpkin only grows if there's a free block next to it. Pumpkins need their space too.
Sprinkle bone meal on grass and flowers grow. Sprinkle it on yourself and nothing happens. I've checked.
Every so often there's a poisonous potato in the harvest. The black sheep of the family.
One of my books has a mirror that shows you what you want most. I'd see emeralds.
A wizard is never late, it says in one of my books. The librarian from the next village always is.
I wanted to sort my books by color. Then I noticed they all look the same.
I sell redstone, lapis and glowstone. Anyone who says faith isn't practical has never visited me.
Potions of invisibility are my bestseller. I just never see who buys them.
When a potion goes wrong, I just call it a potion of experience.
Netherite armor doesn't sink in lava. Whoever's wearing it, sadly, does.
The weaponsmith sells swords, I sell the armor against them. We're business partners, really. Just don't tell him.
A diamond chestplate can take a lot. Not a creeper's bad mood, though.
The toolsmith says an axe is a tool. I say it's a weapon. We've agreed to disagree, loudly.
Pillagers have crossbows and no manners. At least I have manners.
If the fisherman says my swords smell of fish one more time, I'm selling him a blunt one.
A Fortune pickaxe gets you more diamonds. Sadly it doesn't get me more customers.
My anvil's already cracked. A few more repairs and it's done for.
The fisherman says my hammering scares his fish away. As if fish had ears.
I sail the really big ships.
The lads on the street are sacred to me!
Foul weather brings the best fish, that's what I always say.
The smith bangs so loud the fish jump ashore of their own accord. Just for some peace and quiet.
A spectral arrow makes monsters glow. Handy if you want to know what you're running from.
A crossbow shoots further. A bow looks better.
They say someone in the woods takes from the rich and gives to the poor. Emeralds for everyone, so to speak.
Sixteen colors of wool, and still everyone wants white.
A trader once told me: name a sheep jeb_ and it shines in every color.
The sheep eat the grass, the grass grows back, so does the wool. A perfect cycle. Only I get tired.
I sell meat and buy coal. No coal, no fire. No fire, no business.
A campfire cooks slowly, but four pieces at once. Patience pays off.
Everyone asks why I buy sweet berries. I'm not telling. Secret recipe.
Four rabbit hides make one piece of leather. The rabbits see it differently.
You can dye leather armor. Try doing that with diamond.
Nothing ever gets cooked in my cauldron. It's for dyeing, not for soup.
Polished diorite is the most beautiful thing there is. I know not everyone agrees.
I built a wall today. The zombies still found a way around it.
A right angle is my best friend. It's always right.
I once swapped a golden statue for a bag of sand. Shortly after, a stone ball came rolling after me.
My maps only show where I've already been. That's why the world looks so small on them.
I'm keeping an eye on my chest now. Let's see who still dares touch my emeralds.
I thought so hard today that I forgot what about.
My green smock isn't workwear. It's a way of life.
I can count to ten. Sometimes even in the right order.
Without a job I have plenty of time. I just don't know what for.
The moment a smithing table turns up, I'm a toolsmith. Until then, I'm open to anything.
My résumé is short: villager. Always have been.
I drink a potion of invisibility every evening. Purely a precaution.
I sell buckets of fish, cacti and blue ice. I never claimed to have a concept.
My llamas follow me everywhere. They still never pay.
Out here there are more cacti than things to talk about.
On the plains you can spot every zombie from far off. That's both reassuring and unsettling.
The forest smells of moss and oak. And of adventure, if you're not careful.
The wolves here are harmless, as long as you don't owe them a bone.
In the snow you can see every footprint. Even the ones you'd rather not.
In the swamp the water's green and the mood is grey.
In the jungle, cocoa grows on the trees. Why would I ever buy cookies again?
Acacia wood is orange. My house looks like a sunset.
The cliffs here are striped like a layer cake. Sadly, just as hard as stone.
There's supposed to be treasure under the sand. Under this sand or that sand over there. Somewhere, anyway.
No monsters show up here, just cows with mushrooms. I'll take that deal.
I'd like to grow old under the cherry blossoms. Or at least have lunch there.
The meadow up here is so peaceful I almost forget how high up we are.
The sea is so big I wonder if someone on the other side is looking back.
Somewhere in the dark forest there's supposed to be a mansion full of evokers. I'm not knocking.
Birch trees always look like they've dressed up for the occasion.
Tulips bloom here in four colors. I couldn't pick a favorite.
The roots here grow every which way. Like my thoughts before breakfast.
The wind up here always whistles the same tune. I can hum along by now.
This high up the snow never melts. I admire its stamina.
Among the ice spikes I feel like I'm in a frozen forest.
The grove is so quiet you can hear the snow falling.
Dripstone grows slower than my patience runs out.
Moss, berries and leaves everywhere. I almost forget I'm standing in a cave.
If you call out down here, it isn't the echo that answers. It's something else.
Under these giants I feel young. Not many things manage that.
I walk very carefully on the frozen water. You never know who's listening underneath.
Bamboo grows faster than I can harvest it. Finally, something that works harder than me.
If I sit by the river long enough, maybe a salmon swims by. Or a thought.
This is where mountain meets sea. Neither one gives way.
It smells of fungus and trouble around here.
The endermen here are calmer than elsewhere. I still don't look any of them in the eye.
Walk across soul sand and sometimes you hear a sigh. I hope it was mine.
The basalt pillars look like a giant once played the organ here.
Those lost in the icy mountains are said to see a blue bird appear. Articuno. Nobody will tell you if that's a good sign.
There are tales of a bird of fire called Moltres. Every flap of its wings a shower of sparks. It'd feel right at home here.
People used to cross the sea on the back of a Lapras, they say. Nowadays you take a boat. Far less romantic.
I once saw a Gyarados in the water. Ever since, I only go in up to my knees.
Deep down in the sea, Lugia is said to sleep. One flutter of its wings could blow whole houses away. Best let it sleep.
When the forest goes completely quiet, Celebi supposedly drops by from another time. I've been waiting for weeks.
Whoever sees Ho-Oh in the sky is blessed with eternal happiness. So far I've only seen chickens.
Groudon is said to have raised these rocks from the ground when it wanted more land. It was certainly thorough.
Suicune is said to run through the forests on the north wind, purifying every stream it touches.
High above the clouds, they say, lives a green sky serpent. Rayquaza. No wonder it's so windy up here.
Whenever I see a shooting star at night, I think of Jirachi. It's said to wake for seven days every thousand years and grant wishes.
When it rains for days, my grandma says Kyogre has woken up and wants a bigger sea.
Make three sacrifices and you can summon a god, the old folks say. All I've got is three cacti.
Spiders. Why did it have to be spiders?
Lightning struck a pig over there. Now it's a zombified piglin. I'm not making this up.
Trading is like dancing. Just with more emeralds.
Emeralds are worth the most in the morning. At least that's what my gut says.
In the evening I count my emeralds. In the morning I count them again, given what's been going on at the cartographer's.
I only count to 64. After that I start a new stack.
A chunk is sixteen by sixteen blocks. That's 256 good reasons to build neatly.
The cartographer says pi never ends. I asked if that goes for pumpkin pie too.
My financial advisor says: buy wheat while it's cheap. My financial advisor is a chicken.
Not a single emerald went missing at the cartographer's today. That's almost more suspicious.
I hid my emeralds under the bed. Now I can't sleep.
Schmorf, the smith's son, jumped off a roof because it was supposed to look cool. It did not look cool.
Count Thaddäus Montgomery Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach zu Falkenberg introduced himself to me. By the time he finished, it was dark.
I spent ages looking for Earl D. Wilson. He was standing next to me the whole time.
Stanley Balls claimed he could mine stone with his bare hands. He can, too. Very, very slowly.
Sometimes I just want to climb onto the roof and shout: Freedom! Like that Eduard Laser fellow.
Eduard Laser calls his son Lauchboy. Yet the boy's the only one in the family who understands redstone.
A trader swears he saw a ghast that was happy. With a harness and people riding on top.
Rumor has it there are copper golems somewhere that tidy up chests. Nobody tidies anything here.
In some faraway world, people have waited over ten years for the next chapter of a story. And it keeps getting delayed.
Far to the south, the world's best athletes are said to have competed on snow and ice. I'd have slipped during the warm-up.
Last night something big went stomping past my window. And in the morning there was a poppy at the door.
The iron golem spent today pretending to look at the clouds. Very suspicious.
The bell rang again at midnight. I stayed in bed. That's not cowardice, that's experience.
The nitwit swears it wasn't him with the bell. He didn't even know where the bell is.
Last night someone with a shovel and a hat was digging up the field. That's all I could make out in the dark.
I've started keeping a notebook of everything strange in this village. It's almost full.
A trader swears there are green pipes you can slide through into other worlds. All we have is the well.
Touch a glowing star and you're invincible for a while, they say. And afterwards a tune gets stuck in your head forever.
The plumber's younger brother, the one in green, supposedly cleared out a whole haunted mansion. With a vacuum cleaner. Whatever that is.
If a tiny glowing fairy keeps shouting Hey! Listen! in your ear, that's not luck. That's a job.
An old map showed three golden triangles. Power, wisdom and courage. All I found there was sand.
A boy in green cut all the grass outside the village. He swore there were gems underneath.
I tried jumping on a creeper to defeat it. It worked for the plumber. Not for me.
A wanderer played a tune on a little flute, and suddenly it was morning. I'd love that flute for the long nights.
In my books, everyone mixes up the silent hero in green with the princess. Even though she's the one it's all named after.
